stem.en: A crowbar lifts a rock with an effort smaller than the load. A student says: "The crowbar gives out more work than I put in." Where is the student wrong?

text.en: Nowhere. A larger force at the rock means more work.
The rock moves a shorter distance, so the work is the same.
The crowbar spreads the load, so it needs less work.
The rock gains no energy, so no work is done on it.

explanation.en: The crowbar gives a larger force at the rock, but the rock moves a shorter distance than your hand does. Ignoring friction, F1 x d1 = F2 x d2: the work you put in equals the work done on the rock. A lever reduces the force, not the work. The rock does gain potential energy as it rises.

hints.en: How far does each end of the crowbar move?
Work = force x distance, at each end.
